reason: A 1984 immunology review of host defense and biologic-response modifiers, not about LLM agents with tools.
A conceptual monograph on closed-loop quantum health decision systems with no tool-using LLM agent and no attack or utility measurement.
A deep reinforcement learning anomaly detector for cyber-physical systems, not about LLM agents with tools.
An agentic reinforcement learning method that uses action guidance to train search agents, with no adversary, defense or privilege policy.
A system that builds decision knowledge graphs from developer-AI conversations and exposes them through MCP, with no security question.
A position paper arguing that defenders must build offensive AI hacking agents, with no quantitative attack or utility measure of its own.
An essay that traces the everything-is-a-file idea into agentic AI design, with no defense, adversary or measurement.
A 1999 article on Ada compiler validation, not about LLM agents.
Uses an LLM as a network-defense agent in CybORG and distills it into a small RL agent, which is LLM-for-cyber-defense and not a defense of a tool-using LLM agent against adversarial input.
A psychology commentary on master narratives and identity, not about LLM agents.
A survey of LLM jailbreak attacks and defenses whose figures synthesize prior work, mainly on chat models, with no measurement of its own.
A deep reinforcement learning coordination strategy for multi-agent aerospace pick-and-place, not about LLM agents.
An organizational AI implementation plan for CERN, with no tool-using agent security study.
A cost-efficient multi-agent routing framework trained by on-policy distillation, with no adversary, defense or privilege policy.
Proposes a layered prompt-injection defense for agentic AI security workflows and reports detection and false-positive rates on 1,000 adversarial prompts.

Proposes a learned control layer in which a tool-using LLM agent chooses to act or defer to human oversight and shows fewer safety violations on an agentic tool-use task; the adversarial setting is unclear, so it is kept for the full-text check.
A position paper on what LLM agent benchmark scores measure, with no attack, defense or security measure.
Shows that obfuscated malicious agent skills evade static scanners and proposes a sandboxed runtime auditor for coding agents with detection and false-positive rates.
A risks-and-governance paper that describes MCP threats and proposes controls, but its abstract shows no quantitative attack or utility measure of its own.
Benchmarks the security mechanisms of coding agent harnesses and reports attack success beside task utility for settings such as allowlisting, isolation and auto-approve.
A management-science framework for governing agentic AI in performance management, with no tool-using agent security measurement.
Evaluates data leakage by tool-using LLM agents in explicitly non-adversarial tasks and evaluates no defense, so it meets no criterion.
A descriptive book chapter on action-data systems, tool registries and MCP authorization, with no attack or utility measurement of its own.
Uses MCP-named agent communication in an R package for financial systemic-risk modeling, with no LLM agent security question.
A genetic-algorithm model evolution method for multi-task reinforcement learning in robotics, not about LLM agents.
A meta automatic curriculum learning method for deep RL agents, not about LLM agents.
A dissertation on unsupervised target detection in hyperspectral imagery, not about LLM agents.
Replicates an AI agent privilege-escalation incident in containers and evaluates zero-trust least-privilege enforcement that blocks the attack vector.
A systematic review of defenses against prompt-based attacks in LLM agents, with a descriptive synthesis and no measurement of its own.
Shows that Unicode TAG-block payloads in MCP tool metadata reach the model while hidden from the approval view, and tests a sanitizer against the attack techniques and benign descriptions.
A case study of AI-enabled nuclear safety documentation, not about the security of tool-using LLM agents.
Proposes type-directed privilege separation as a system-level prompt-injection defense for LLM agents and reports security with non-trivial utility.
A criminology article on globalization, borders and transnational crime, not about LLM agents.
A curriculum method for LLM reinforcement fine-tuning, tested also on function-calling benchmarks, with no adversary or defense.
A history chapter on agrarian power and poverty in colonial Bihar, not about LLM agents.
An environmental-policy essay on narratives of degradation, not about LLM agents.
A special-issue editorial on air warfare simulation reuse and interoperability, not about LLM agents.
Proposes an identity and authority architecture for multi-user agent systems, but the abstract reports no attack or utility evaluation, so it reads as a design or position paper.
A benchmark of agent harness configurations across models on realistic workflows, which is a tool-use benchmark with no adversary.
A teacher-guided policy optimization method for tool learning in small language models, with no adversary or defense.
A special-issue introduction on participatory action research with children, not about LLM agents.
A regional-geography study of Lisbon and Gothenburg strategy implementation in Italian provinces, not about LLM agents.
A technical report on a mixture-of-experts LLM, with no agent security study.
Connects local LLMs to Burp Suite through MCP to automate penetration testing and measures capability, which is not an attack on or a defense of the agent or MCP.
A benchmark and RAG method for LLM assistants in electric power marketing, with no tools-security question.
Optimizes shared tool descriptions and implementations from agent traces to raise task success, which learns no policy or permission set and has no adversary.
An editorial on cyber statecraft and national cyber governance, not about LLM agents.
A review of prompt injection attacks and defenses with no quantitative attack or utility measure of its own.
A routing framework that learns agent capability profiles from traffic to improve routing accuracy, which is not a security policy and has no adversary.
A 2012 policy essay on which U.S. agency should lead cybersecurity, not about LLM agents.
